instruct: An elderly woman in her eighties, warm and slightly frail, speaking slowly and a little too loudly, as if a bit hard of hearing.
ref_text: Hello? Oh, the phone always rings when I'm in the garden. Speak up, dear, I can't hear a thing on this old thing.

instruct: A gruff, tired middle-aged man with a low gravelly voice, flat and unimpressed, speaking in short clipped words.
ref_text: Yeah. I just got home. I've been on my feet for ten hours and the last thing I need is another phone call.

instruct: A cheerful young man in his early twenties, relaxed and upbeat, a laid-back surfer energy, speaking quickly.
ref_text: Oh hey, what's up? Sorry, I was totally just making a sandwich, but yeah, go for it, I've got like a minute.

instruct: A brisk professional woman in her forties, crisp, clipped and impatient, clearly busy, mid-range voice.
ref_text: This is Linda. I'm between two meetings and I have exactly ninety seconds, so whatever this is, get to the point.

instruct: A suspicious old man in his seventies, raspy and thin, slow and wary, distrustful of everything.
ref_text: Who is this? How did you get this number? I don't give my number to anybody, and I don't like this one bit.

instruct: A bored teenage girl, flat monotone, unimpressed, drawling slightly, a young high voice.
ref_text: Hello? Yeah, no, nobody's home. I mean, I'm home, but I don't count. Can you, like, call back later or something?

instruct: A nervous, soft-spoken man in his thirties, a slightly high voice, hesitant and apologetic, stumbling over words.
ref_text: Oh. Um. Hello? Sorry, I don't usually answer the phone, I wasn't sure if, um, if I should. Is everything okay?

instruct: A very deep-voiced man who has just been woken up, slow, groggy and sleepy, low and mumbling.
ref_text: Mmh... hello? I was asleep. I work nights. It's the middle of my night right now, you understand that, right?

instruct: A warm, chatty middle-aged woman with a friendly sing-song voice and a gentle Southern drawl, delighted to talk.
ref_text: Well hi there! Oh, I just love getting calls, nobody calls anymore. Now what can I do for you today, sweetheart?

instruct: A man in his forties with a heavy head cold, congested and nasal, sniffling, miserable and weak.
ref_text: Hello? Sorry, I sound terrible, I've had this cold for a week and I can barely breathe through my nose at all.

instruct: A young mother whispering very softly and urgently, breathy and hushed, trying not to wake a sleeping baby.
ref_text: Hello? Please keep your voice down. The baby just fell asleep, and it took me two hours to get her down.

instruct: A jovial man in his fifties with a deep, low bass voice, hearty and booming, slow and over the top like an old-fashioned car salesman. Low pitch.
ref_text: Yello! You got me, buddy! Talk to me, I love a good phone call, whatever you're selling I'm all ears, pal!

instruct: A corporate supervisor, a smooth, calm, cold mid-low voice, perfectly even and unhurried, polite on the surface and quietly menacing underneath.
ref_text: This is your supervisor. I trust the calls are going well. I see every number you dial, and I remember all of them.
